preheader: CVS splits up, Damodaran cuts Anthropic valuation, and Rafael Nadal joins Real Madrid.

lead.headline: CVS Health Plans Massive Split to Reverse Aetna Deal
lead.body: CVS Health announced plans to split into two separate public companies by the first half of 2028. This move effectively reverses its $78 billion acquisition of Aetna and dismantles the vertically integrated healthcare conglomerate created in 2018.
lead.why: This is a massive case study in corporate strategy and portfolio restructuring for your business classes. It shows how conglomerates sometimes unwind big mergers when the expected synergies do not pan out.

figures.label: Separate public companies to be formed

stories.headline: Datadog Beats Q3 Estimates But Shares Plunge on Weak Guidance
stories.body: Datadog reported Q3 earnings that beat Wall Street estimates, but its shares tanked because Q4 revenue guidance fell short and signaled flat sequential growth.
stories.why: A great lesson in equity research for your investing interest. It proves that forward-looking guidance often matters far more to the market than past performance.

stories.headline: Aswath Damodaran Trims Anthropic Valuation to $1.45 Trillion
stories.body: Valuation expert Aswath Damodaran lowered his estimated worth for Anthropic to $1.45 trillion, citing concerns over governance, regulatory hurdles, infrastructure costs, and profitability.
stories.why: Paying attention to how the Dean of Valuation values pre-IPO AI giants will help you build solid financial models for your finance coursework.

stories.headline: Terawulf Secures Credit Backstop From Google for Data Center Project
stories.body: Data-center developer Terawulf secured a credit backstop agreement with Alphabet's Google to support financing for its $19 billion data center lease commitment.
stories.why: Shows how tech giants are directly backing massive infrastructure and energy projects to secure the compute power needed for AI scaling.

stories.headline: Generative Media Startup Fal Raises $1.3 Billion at a $16 Billion Valuation
stories.body: Generative media inference startup fal raised $1.3 billion in new funding at a valuation of $16 billion. The company plans to spend the capital on computing power and hiring.
stories.why: A massive data point for startup and venture capital funding trends, showing that investors are still writing huge checks for infrastructure-heavy AI plays.

stories.headline: McKinsey Warns of Global Climate Adaptation Costs for Emerging Economies
stories.body: A new McKinsey report highlights that India could need to spend up to 3 percent of its GDP annually on climate adaptation, compared to just 0.5 percent in wealthier economies.
stories.why: Useful for consulting frameworks and macro strategy, showing how physical risk and climate economics will force developing nations to allocate capital differently.

stories.headline: Former McKinsey Consultant Publishes Book on the Human Side of Consulting
stories.body: As AI reshapes entry-level tasks at consulting firms, a new book by a former McKinsey consultant looks at the human coaching and advisory skills that software cannot replace.
stories.why: If you are aiming for a career in consulting, it highlights how the industry is pivoting toward interpersonal skills as AI takes over backend analysis.

stories.headline: UC Irvine Men's Basketball Rolls Past Chapman 92-66 in Season Opener
stories.body: UC Irvine opened its season with a dominant 92-66 win over Chapman at the Bren Events Center, led by 16 points from debutant Luke Isaak and a double-double from 7-foot-9 Olivier Rioux.

stories.headline: Rafael Nadal Appointed to Board of Directors at Real Madrid
stories.body: Twenty-two-time tennis Grand Slam champion Rafael Nadal is set to join the board of directors at his boyhood football club, Real Madrid, pending member ratification.

term.name: Forward Guidance
term.definition: Forward guidance is a company's official forecast of its future business performance and revenue, given to the public and investors during earnings reports. Today's news about Datadog shows why guidance is so powerful: even though their past quarter beat expectations, a weak outlook caused the stock to drop sharply.

serve.headline: Shackleton AI raised $5M from Battery Ventures to automate construction projects
serve.body: New York-based Shackleton AI emerged from stealth with $5 million in seed funding led by Battery Ventures to build AI agents that handle administrative work in construction. The company's platform already manages over $1 billion in project value.
questions: How can an early-stage B2B startup prove enterprise value when managing over $1 billion in assets with a team just coming out of stealth?
What customer acquisition strategy works best when selling workflow automation to traditional industries like construction?
How would you price an AI agent platform that saves administrative hours across massive capital projects?
